title: Operadic colimits fill active join boundaries ending at a color
statement: Use symmetric infinity-operads and operadically $q$-colimiting cocones of [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family], and ordered joins of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Let $q:E^\otimes\to O^\otimes$ be a cocartesian fibration and an inert-preserving map of symmetric infinity-operads. Let $K$ be any small simplicial set, $r>0$, and let $a:K\star\partial\Delta^r\to E^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$ and $b:K\star\Delta^r\to O^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$ satisfy $qa=b|_{K\star\partial\Delta^r}$. Suppose $a|_{K\star\{0\}}$ is operadically $q$-colimiting and $a(r)$ lies over $\langle1\rangle$. Then there exists $h:K\star\Delta^r\to E^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$ with $h|_{K\star\partial\Delta^r}=a$ and $qh=b$ exactly. The initial apex may have arbitrary arity, $K$ may be empty, and no colimits other than the indicated cocone are assumed.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.7, printed pp.319-320, direction (1) to (2); operadic colimiting implies weak operadic colimiting by Definition 3.1.1.2. September 18, 2017 edition inspected online. WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text: Put $C=E^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$, $D=O^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$, $f=a|_K$, and $c=a|_{K\star\{0\}}$. The active subcategories are pullbacks of the operads along $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*^{\mathrm{act}})\subseteq N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$, so they are quasicategories by the operads' inner-horn axiom. The restriction $q_C:C\to D$ is an inner fibration: fill a horn using $q$, and the resulting simplex is active because its image in $D$ is active and $q$ preserves the pointed-set coordinate. Write $R=C_{f/}$ and $S=D_{qf/}$ for the sharp join coslices. Their simplices and the join adjunction are those of [lem-coef-infinity-join-cocone-associativity]. The relative coslice lemma [lem-cbc-relative-coslice-left-fibration], applied to $\varnothing\hookrightarrow K$, factors $Q:R\to S$ as the left fibration $R\to C\times_D S$ followed by the pullback of $q_C$. Pullbacks and composites of inner fibrations lift inner horns successively, so $Q$ is an inner fibration between quasicategories. The given maps correspond exactly to $u:\partial\Delta^r\to R$ and $v:\Delta^r\to S$, with $Qu=v|_{\partial\Delta^r}$ and $u(0)=c$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.7 proof, pp.319–320: active coslices and the inner fibration q-prime; HTT Proposition 2.1.2.1 as exposed by the relative coslice lemma.

proof.text:
Let $C_1\subseteq C$ be the full subcategory on the color objects, and form the actual relative restriction
$$\psi:C_1\times_C C_{c/}\longrightarrow C_1\times_C\bigl(C_{f/}\times_{D_{qf/}}D_{qc/}\bigr).$$
The relative coslice lemma, for $K\hookrightarrow K\star\{0\}$, makes this a left fibration. For a diagram $d:T\to C$ and a vertex $W$, write $U_d(W)=C_{d/}\times_C\{W\}$; use the analogous notation in $D$. Apply [lem-coef-cone-apex-cocone-space-comparison] to $c$ and $q_C$. For every color $W$, it identifies the square with rows $U_c(W)\to U_f(W)$ and $U_{qc}(qW)\to U_{qf}(qW)$ with the mapping-space square whose upper row is $\operatorname{Map}_C(c(0),W)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,C)}(f,\Delta_KW)$, given by composition with the coherent cocone $c$. The comparison retains the composition homotopy in the lower square.

source.place: Definition 3.1.1.2 and Remark 3.1.1.5, pp.318–319: weak operadic restriction is a trivial Kan fibration; mapping-space translation of the empty-concatenation case.

proof.text: Take the empty tuple $Z$ in the operadic hypothesis of [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family]. The coherent unit of concatenation in [lem-coef-active-operad-cocartesian-concatenation], preserved by $q$, identifies $c\oplus1_Z$ with $c$ and the source diagram with $f$. Thus the resulting mapping-space square for every color $W$ is a homotopy pullback. By the square comparison of Step 2, including its specified composition homotopy, the square with rows $U_c(W)\to U_f(W)$ and $U_{qc}(qW)\to U_{qf}(qW)$ is a homotopy pullback as well. Homotopy pullback invariance justifies the unit-equivalence replacements in its three testing corners. Only colors $W$ are used; no relative initiality against arbitrary tuple apexes is asserted.

source.place: Definition 3.1.1.2 and Remark 3.1.1.5, pp.318–319: weak operadic restriction is a trivial Kan fibration; mapping-space translation of the empty-concatenation case.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-relative-coslice-homotopy-pullback-test] with $A=K$, $B=K\star\{0\}$, $d=c$, $e=f$, and full subcategory $C_0=C_1$. The map $q_C$ is an inner fibration by Step 1, the shape inclusion is degreewise injective, and Step 3 supplies its homotopy-pullback hypothesis at every vertex of $C_1$. Hence the actual map $\psi$ lifts every boundary, including dimension zero. The sharp-join associator gives $C_{c/}\cong R_{c/}$ and $D_{qc/}\cong S_{Qc/}$, preserving projections and restrictions. Consequently this is an exact relative coslice lift whenever the remaining apex vertices are colors.

source.place: Definition 3.1.1.2 and Remark 3.1.1.5, pp.318–319: weak operadic restriction is a trivial Kan fibration; mapping-space translation of the empty-concatenation case.

proof.text:
Define $t:\Delta^r\times\Delta^1\to\Delta^r$ by $t(i,0)=i$ and $t(i,1)=r$. This is monotone on the product poset. Set
$$X=(\partial\Delta^r\times\{0\})\cup(\Lambda_r^r\times\Delta^1)\cup(\Delta^r\times\{1\}).$$
On the middle part every simplex omits a vertex different from $r$, so its image under $t$ is in $\partial\Delta^r$; the top part maps to $r$. Thus $g_0=u\circ t|_X$ is defined and lies over $v\circ t$. In particular the top face is constant at $z=u(r)$, whose apex is the prescribed color $a(r)$, and the vertical edge at $r$ is degenerate at $z$. On the bottom boundary $g_0=u$. We extend this particular map, leaving $X$ fixed throughout.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.7 proof, pp.319–320: the collapse r and the initial subset X of the prism.

proof.text:
For $1\leq i\leq r$, adjoin to the current subset the $r$-simplex $\sigma_i$ with vertices
$$\sigma_i(j)=\begin{cases}(j,0)&j\leq r-i,\\(j-1,1)&j>r-i.\end{cases}$$
For $i<r$ its intersection with the preceding subset is precisely $\Lambda_{r-i}^r$: deleting any vertex other than $r-i$ leaves a face in $X$ or in an earlier $\sigma_j$, while deletion of $r-i$ is the new face. The index satisfies $0<r-i<r$, so the inner fibration $Q$ of Step 1 extends the map over this simplex, over the fixed map $v\circ t$. At $i=r$ the intersection is instead the full $\partial\Delta^r$. Indeed the zeroth face lies in the top face, the first face was adjoined at $i=r-1$ when $r>1$, and each other face lies in $\Lambda_r^r\times\Delta^1$ because its first-coordinate support omits a vertex different from $r$. For $r=1$ both endpoints are already in $X$. This corrects the printed zeroth-horn pushout at $i=r$ in HA 3.1.1.7(i). The initial vertex of $\sigma_r$ is $c$ and all its remaining vertices lie in the top face, with color apex $a(r)$. The entire prescribed boundary, together with the base simplex, is therefore a boundary lifting problem $\partial\Delta^{r-1}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{r-1}$ for $\psi$ of Step 4: the top face gives the target simplex, and its remaining faces give the source boundary, by the sharp-join associator. The trivial Kan fibration $\psi$ fills it, including dimension zero when $r=1$. Thus the full $\sigma_r$ can be attached with every already prescribed face unchanged.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.7 proof, p.320, part (i): the r-dimensional simplices; corrected final attachment is a full boundary, as detailed in report.md under Source error.

proof.text:
Next, for $1\leq j\leq r+1$, adjoin the $(r+1)$-simplex $\tau_j$ with vertices
$$\tau_j(k)=\begin{cases}(k,0)&k<j,\\(k-1,1)&k\geq j.\end{cases}$$
Its intersection with what is already attached is $\Lambda_j^{r+1}$: all faces except deletion of vertex $j$ are in the initial subset or in earlier listed simplices. The $\tau_j$ are the maximal simplices of $\Delta^r\times\Delta^1$, so the resulting subset is the whole prism. For $j\leq r$ the horn is inner and is filled using $Q$. For $j=r+1$ the final edge is the vertical edge at $r$, which $g_0$ already sent to the degenerate edge at $z$. It is an equivalence. Apply the final-horn clause of [lem-cbc-inner-fibration-equivalence-outer-horn-lift] to $Q$ to fill this last simplex over $v\circ t$. We obtain $g:\Delta^r\times\Delta^1\to R$ extending $g_0$ exactly and satisfying $Qg=v\circ t$ exactly.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.7 proof, pp.320–321, part (ii): the maximal prism simplices and final equivalence edge.

proof.text: Restrict $g$ to $\Delta^r\times\{0\}$. Because $t|_{\Delta^r\times\{0\}}$ is the identity and the bottom boundary belongs to $X$, this gives $\widetilde u:\Delta^r\to R$ with $Q\widetilde u=v$ and $\widetilde u|_{\partial\Delta^r}=u$. The natural bijection of [lem-coef-infinity-join-cocone-associativity] turns it into $h:K\star\Delta^r\to C$; its naturality in the indexing simplicial set and in $q_C$ gives the two required equalities exactly. No equivalence of cocone models is being used to turn a homotopy into an equality at this step. If $K=\varnothing$, the sharp coslices are $C,D$ themselves and every construction remains defined. For $r=1$ the two horn phases are respectively a color-target edge lift and a $2$-simplex lift with degenerate final edge. The initial apex arity was unrestricted throughout: only $z$ was required to have color apex in Step 6. The argument used only the empty-concatenation consequence of the specified operadic cocone, and no other colimits.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.7 proof, pp.320–321: restriction to the bottom prism face; Definition 3.1.1.2 includes arbitrary initial arity and empty K.

I checked the route against my knowledge of HA Def 3.1.1.2, Rem 3.1.1.5 and Prop 3.1.1.7 (1)=>(2), and against the Q18 reviewer's record of those pages. I read all eight steps and the full statements of the 12 cited nodes. Step 1: active subcategory pullback and q_C inner are elementary; the relative-coslice lemma with K_0 empty gives R->C x_D S. Step 2: psi is a left fibration via K in K^cone; I checked the hypotheses of the new cone-apex node. Step 3: the operadic hypothesis at the empty Z, via the unitor of the concatenation lemma, gives a homotopy pullback at colors only. Applying the invariance lemma after a standard rectification is acceptable. Step 4: hypotheses of the new criterion node hold at A=K, B=K^cone, C_0=C_1, and the associator is natural. Prism: my own script confirms, for r=1..7, inner horns Lambda^r_{r-i} for i<r, the full boundary at i=r (HA's printed Lambda_0 is wrong there; the source correction is kept), Lambda^{r+1}_j for the tau_j, and full coverage. The last tau uses the final-horn equivalence lift; sigma_r is a boundary lift for psi, including dimension 0 at r=1. Both new nodes are true and statement-only. The cone-apex comparison holds by right-anodyne apex restriction plus the join-slice comparison; checked at K empty and q=id. The criterion holds because the fiberwise map is a Kan fibration and w.e., so a left fibration with contractible fibers is a trivial fibration; checked at q=id, C_0 empty and D=point. Neither duplicates constant-test, join-slice-comparison, cofinal-restriction or relative-initial-boundary, and neither restates a clause of the item. No cycle; stmt_deps and four search kinds are present; blueprint ancestry is inherited.
